problem: Image-goal Visual Navigation Models (VNMs such as NoMaD) need a dense, traversable sequence of target point-of-view images from start to goal. Image-based topological graphs (ITG) built from sparse image databases lack start/goal nodes, give detours, and cost storage that grows linearly with the number of images.
motivation: In settings like exhibition halls or stores, data collection is expensive because the environment changes and survey time is limited. VNMs avoid precise localization, but still need dense image coverage. 3DGS is compact and can render novel views, so it can synthesize the missing intermediate viewpoints.
key_idea: Replace the ITG with a 3D Gaussian Splatting map that is used offline to localize the start and goal images, plan a path with A*, and render a dense sequence of target views that a pretrained NoMaD policy follows without online localization.
insight: Rendering intermediate views removes the dependence on image DB density. SPL stays high down to about 500 images, while NoMaD w/ ITG degrades sharply on sparse DBs, and the method can reach observed-but-unvisited rooms. Table I shows SR gains come from better pose estimation (PE-SR) and coverage, but ITG views are easier for NoMaD to track (higher VF-SR), so tracking of rendered views is the bottleneck.
method: 3DGS environment model: Splatfacto (Nerfstudio) trained on the image DB with COLMAP point-cloud initialization; Gaussians are converted to ellipsoids for ellipsoid-to-sphere distance and collision checks (robot radius set as a hyperparameter, 0.01 in 3DGS units).

Start/goal pose estimation: one-shot global search over (x, y, yaw) minimizing an LPIPS loss between the given image and the rendered image plus a collision penalty, using TPE black-box optimization (Optuna). z, roll and pitch are fixed to the mean of the DB camera poses.
Global trajectory planning: A* in 3DGS over x-y with collision checks, then yaw assigned via atan2 along the path. Hybrid A* performed similarly.
Target view rendering: 3DGS renders images along the planned trajectory, giving a dense sequence Vr ending with the goal image.

NoMaD zero-shot local policy: the distance head finds the nearest rendered image to the current observation, and the next image is used as subgoal. The diffusion policy outputs 8 waypoints, tracked by MPPI with a differential-drive model.

setting.backbone: NoMaD (pretrained, frozen, authors' weights) + 3DGS (Splatfacto, per-scene optimization) + MPPI
setting.training_data: NoMaD pretrained on large heterogeneous robot datasets (~100 hours, no Habitat data); 3DGS fitted per scene on 300-3000 collected images
setting.observation: monocular RGB (1280x720, 120° FOV, height 0.4 m); start and goal images given
setting.action_space: continuous linear/angular velocity (max 0.25 m/s, 0.5 rad/s) via MPPI tracking NoMaD waypoints
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson scenes Greigsville, Ribera; Habitat test scene skokloster-castle)
setting.privileged: none at test time beyond a pre-collected image DB (images collected by NoMaD exploration); simulator traversable map only used for evaluation

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 trials per env and DB size; Table I aggregated over image DB sizes

numbers_note: SPL results are only shown as box plots in Fig. 3 (no numeric values). Table I SR values are printed as 0-1 fractions. Storage results are in Table II (3DGS 508/530/442/223 MB vs ITG 322/840/2300/3400 MB for 300/1000/2000/3000 images).
results: GSplatVNM achieves the highest SR in all three scenes (0.55, 0.40, 0.59), versus 0.47/0.42, 0.30/0.27 and 0.34/0.39 for NoMaD w/o ITG and w/ ITG. On skokloster-castle its SR is about 20 points above NoMaD w/ ITG. It also keeps higher SPL on sparse DBs and uses far less storage at large DB sizes (223 MB vs 3400 MB at 3000 images).
limitations: Assumes planar 2D motion, so it does not handle ramps or multiple floors.

Collision checking on 3DGS is metrically imprecise, and NoMaD tracks rendered views less reliably (lower VF-SR than ITG). Pose estimation can confuse similar-looking places, and very small DBs degrade rendering quality.
